creator_or_organization: Ben Thompson (MBA from Northwestern Kellogg, Master of Engineering Management from McCormick School; former Apple intern at Apple University, former Microsoft Windows Apps team, former Automattic growth engineer; based in Taiwan; creator of Aggregation Theory; cohosts Sharp Tech, Dithering, and Exponent podcasts)
content_focus: Tech strategy analysis with increasingly dominant AI coverage since 2023. The 2025 Stratechery Year in Review was, like 2024 and 2023, completely dominated by AI. Thompson analyzes AI through a strategic and business lens: how Big Tech companies (Apple, Microsoft, Meta, Google, Amazon) are positioning around AI, the competitive dynamics between OpenAI, DeepSeek, Anthropic and others, AI infrastructure investment and CapEx cycles, the impact of AI on software business models ('SaaSmageddon'), AI integration vs modularization patterns, Apple Intelligence and its platform strategy, semiconductor supply chains (TSMC, Nvidia), and the broader societal implications of AI. Beyond AI, Stratechery covers tech industry structure, media business models, antitrust/regulation, and platform economics. Thompson's signature contribution is applying rigorous strategic frameworks (especially Aggregation Theory) to understand why technology markets evolve the way they do. He also covers enterprise philosophy, national security implications of AI, and the shifting economics of cloud/AI infrastructure.
target_audience: Business leaders, tech executives, venture capitalists, investors, product managers, founders, and strategy-minded professionals. Subscribers span 85+ countries and include C-suite executives at both tech companies and industries being disrupted by technology. Particularly valuable for those who need to understand the 'why' behind tech/AI developments rather than just the 'what'. Accessible to MBA-level readers without deep technical backgrounds.
publication_frequency: 4x per week: 1 free Weekly Article (Tuesdays) + 3 subscriber-only Daily Updates (Mon, Wed, Thu/Fri). Also produces multiple podcasts weekly: Sharp Tech (with Andrew Sharp), Dithering (with John Gruber), Greatest of All Talk, and periodic Stratechery Interviews.
format_and_length: Weekly Articles are long-form analytical essays (typically 15-25 minute reads, 3,000-5,000+ words) with original diagrams and strategic frameworks. Daily Updates are shorter but substantial (10-15 minute reads) covering 2-3 topics with analysis. All written content is also available as audio via podcast feed. The writing style is distinctive: methodical argument-building with historical context, often using the 'situation-complication-resolution' structure. Articles frequently include original diagrams illustrating market dynamics.
accessibility_for_non_engineers: High. Thompson's MBA background and deliberate focus on business strategy rather than technical implementation makes Stratechery exceptionally accessible to non-engineers. He explains technical concepts through their business implications and strategic consequences rather than through code or architecture. His writing 'seamlessly blends sophisticated analysis with accessibility, making complex industry trends understandable and engaging to a wide audience.' Business school students would find his strategic framing, use of frameworks like Aggregation Theory, and emphasis on market dynamics very natural. When he discusses AI models or infrastructure, the focus is always on what it means for businesses, not how the technology works internally.
signal_to_noise_ratio: High. Thompson is widely regarded as one of the highest signal-to-noise ratio writers in tech. Every piece contains original analysis rather than summarizing news. The New York Times called Stratechery 'one of the most interesting sources of analysis on any subject.' Thompson's approach is depth over breadth: he picks 1-3 topics per piece and analyzes them thoroughly rather than covering everything superficially. There is virtually no filler content.
unique_value_proposition: The gold standard for strategic analysis of the tech industry and increasingly of AI. Thompson's unique contribution is applying rigorous, original strategic frameworks to understand technology markets. Aggregation Theory, which he developed, has been called 'the most important business framework of the last 20 years.' No other publication matches his combination of: (1) original strategic frameworks consistently applied over a decade+, (2) deep historical context for every development, (3) business-strategy focus that bridges tech and business audiences, (4) independence from institutional bias (one-person operation with no advertisers or corporate owner), and (5) a track record of prescient analysis. His coverage of AI specifically stands out for framing the AI revolution through competitive strategy, platform dynamics, and historical tech industry patterns rather than hype or fear.
free_or_paid: Freemium. Free tier: 1 Weekly Article per week (high-quality long-form analysis). Paid tier (Stratechery Plus): $15/month or $150/year. Paid includes 3 Daily Updates/week, all podcast access (Sharp Tech, Dithering, Greatest of All Talk, Stratechery Interviews), full archive access, and community features. Previously $12/month or $120/year before a price increase around 2023-2024.
source_reliability: High. Thompson has built a 12+ year track record of rigorous, well-sourced analysis. His independence (no corporate owner, no advertisers, fully subscriber-funded) removes common conflicts of interest. He clearly distinguishes his opinions from facts and regularly revisits and updates his positions when new information emerges. His frameworks (particularly Aggregation Theory) have been validated by industry adoption and academic citation. He acknowledges uncertainty and competing viewpoints. His background (Apple, Microsoft, Automattic + MBA) gives him both insider understanding and analytical rigor. The main caveat is that all analysis reflects one person's perspective, though that perspective has proven remarkably consistent and prescient. Cited by major publications (NYT, WSJ, Bloomberg) and tech executives as an authoritative voice.
relevance_for_entrepreneurs: Extremely relevant for AI entrepreneurs. Thompson provides the strategic frameworks needed to understand where value is being created and captured in the AI ecosystem. His analysis helps entrepreneurs answer critical questions: Should you build on OpenAI's platform or use open-source models? How will AI affect your industry's value chain? What does the 'SaaSmageddon' mean for software startups? How are Big Tech companies positioning, and where are the gaps? His Aggregation Theory framework directly explains platform dynamics that AI entrepreneurs must navigate. His coverage of AI business models, enterprise adoption patterns, build-vs-buy dynamics, and competitive positioning between AI labs provides strategic context that is difficult to find elsewhere. For business school students specifically, Thompson's MBA-flavored analysis translates tech industry dynamics into familiar strategic management concepts.
actionable_insight_level: Medium-High. Stratechery excels at strategic insight rather than tactical how-to advice. Thompson provides frameworks for thinking about technology markets that inform long-term business decisions: where to position a company, how to evaluate competitive threats, when to build vs buy. This is not a 'use this tool' or 'implement this workflow' newsletter. The actionable value is at the strategic level: understanding market dynamics, competitive positioning, and where value is flowing in the AI ecosystem. For entrepreneurs making big-picture decisions about market entry, business model design, or competitive strategy, the insights are highly actionable. For day-to-day operational decisions, less so.
session_mapping: Cross-session, with strongest alignment to S1 (Fundamentals) and S4 (Business Models). S1: provides deep understanding of the AI ecosystem, value chains, and industry structure through strategic frameworks. S3: AI project strategy, build-vs-buy analysis, enterprise adoption patterns. S4: AI business model analysis, platform economics, Aggregation Theory applied to AI markets, competitive dynamics between AI companies. S5: covers AI governance, regulation, and societal impact when strategically relevant (EU AI Act implications, AI and national security).
ecosystem_position: Premier independent analytical voice in tech strategy. Stratechery occupies a unique position as the most influential independent tech strategy publication, sitting between primary news sources (The Information, Bloomberg) and academic analysis. It is an analytical layer that takes news and events and extracts strategic meaning through original frameworks. Thompson is frequently cited by major publications, tech executives, and investors as a key influence on how the industry understands itself. In the AI information landscape specifically, Stratechery provides the strategic 'so what' layer: while other sources report on AI developments or explain the technology, Thompson explains what it means for market structure, competitive dynamics, and business strategy. With an estimated 40,000+ paid subscribers generating $5M+ in annual revenue, Stratechery also serves as a proof-of-concept for the independent newsletter business model that many AI newsletters have since emulated.
